claim: 연간 100개 이하 생산분, 시험용 시제품은 UN 38.3 시험 등 일부 요건 면제
evidence: https://wwwcdn.imo.org/localresources/en/KnowledgeCentre/IndexofIMOResolutions/MSCResolutions/MSC.556(108).pdf — IMDG SP 310: "Cells or batteries from production runs of not more than 100 cells or batteries, or pre-production prototypes of cells or batteries when these prototypes are transported for testing, shall meet the provisions of 2.9.4 with the exception of 2.9.4.1, ..." P910 and LP905 also say "production runs consisting of not more than 100 cells or batteries", with no annual qualifier. "Annual production runs" is the air wording of A88 (https://www.iata.org/contentassets/05e6d8742b0047259bf3a700bc9d42b9/lithium-battery-guidance-document.pdf B.04).
fix: 100개 이하 생산분, 시험을 위해 운송하는 시제품은 UN 38.3 시험 등 일부 요건 면제

evidence: 12 problems: 4 wrong, 3 outdated, 3 overreach, 2 unsupported, 0 unverifiable. Key issues: (1) four internal references say '(5절)' but damaged, recalled and waste batteries and prototypes are covered in section 6. (2) The air PI table leaves out the 3m/24h stack-test requirement that has applied since January 2025 to PI 966 II, 967 I/II, 969 II and 970 I/II. (3) 'Annual' (연간) 100-unit production runs comes from air A88; IMDG SP 310 has no annual qualifier. (4) The SMGS Annex 2 '2025. 1. 1.' date was misread from an ERA entry whose date belongs to RID 2025. (5) One SW19 sentence drops the short-international-voyage exception. (6) 'A201 approvals are rare in practice' is opinion. Sources fetched fresh on 2026-10-19 with curl or WebFetch, no browser: IATA LBGD 2026, IATA DGR 67 Significant Changes, IATA 3m stack-test note, IMO MSC.556(108) full text, OTIF RID 2025 signed PDF, Korean Air KE Variation 2026 PDF and notice node/9349, FAA Lithium Battery Shipping Guide 2026, ERA SMGS Annex 2 entry, and law.go.kr DRF. law.go.kr confirms 항공위험물운송기술기준 고시 2023-52 (시행 2023. 1. 18.), 위험물 선박운송 기준 고시 2026-67 (시행 2026. 6. 21.) and 위험물 선박운송 및 저장규칙 부령 486 (시행 2022. 5. 18.) as the current versions. Checked and correct: all UN numbers and PSNs (3480/3481/3090/3091/3551/3552/3556/3557/3558/3536/3171, plus DGR 68 UN 3563/3564); the texts of IMDG 42-24 SP 188/230/310 (apart from 'annual')/348/360/376/377/384/387/388/389/390/961/962; P903/P908/P909/P910/P911/LP903/LP904; the DGL 3480 row (LQ 0, E0, F-A S-I, Category A, SW19, no SG code); the 7.2.4 Class 9 row (all X); 5.2.1.10 (old mark allowed until 31 Dec 2026); 2.9.4.7 (manufactured after 30 June 2003); 5.4.2.1; entry into force on 1 Jan 2026; RID SP 636 (500 g, 333 kg, P909); all LBGD PI 965-970 limits, IMP codes and the Section IA/IB/I/II structure; the SoC 30% table, including the 2.7 Wh, 100 Wh and IBC 25% rules and the 1 Jan 2026 date; FAQ A.04/A.06/A.07, B.02/B.04, C.05/C.10, D.01-D.06, E.05/E.09/E.10, F.01-F.12, G.01-G.04 and H.01/H.02; the 10 test-summary items; KE-01/03/04/06/08; and 국내 제63조의2, 제99조제15항, 제4조의3, 제16조, 제34조 and the 별표 리튬배터리 부표찰. Per-package limits are net battery weight (FAA guide: PI 965 IB '10 kg net per package', PI 968 IB '2.5 kg net'). The Section I Class 9 label, listed as an inference in facts.md, is confirmed by the FAA guide. Links: all data-doc ids exist in doc_ids.txt and /library/eu-lithium-battery/{status,b-anx14,checklist} exist. The law.go.kr, ERA, IMO, IATA, OTIF and Korean Air URLs return 200 and open the right documents. No advice tells forwarders to inspect cargo physically: forwarders work from documents, and physical checks are assigned to warehouse and packing staff. Sibling docs: consistent with case-accident (OZ991 recommendation), case-litigation (House B/L shipper liability), dg-msds §5, dg-rules and dg-forwarder (고시 2023-52).
